nodes.name: Solvothermal growth
nodes.procedure: The NiMoO4 nano-needle is grown on NF via the solvothermal method.
nodes.source_text: firstly, the NiMoO4 nano-needle is grown on NF via the solvothermal method... which can be determined by XRD (Supplementary Figure S19).

nodes.name: High temperature reduction and carbonization
nodes.procedure: The NiMoO4 nano-needle is reduced by the high temperature (450 °C) calcination in a mixed atmosphere (5% H2 + 95% Ar) to form the Ni nanoparticle and MoO2 nano-needle. The segregated Ni catalyzes the organic carbon to form CN (N-doped carbon), resulting in CN layer coated Ni/MoO2 nano-needle.

unit_operations.name: Calcination
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: reduced by the high temperature (450 °C) calcination in a mixed atmosphere (5% H2 + 95% Ar)

unit_operations.name: Ni-catalyzed carbonization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the segregated Ni can catalyze the organic carbon to form CN... Raman proves the existing of CN, which can be ascribed to the reduction of organic carbon to CN [the ratio of area D and G (Area_D and Area_G) is 1.20]

nodes.source_text: Then, the NiMoO4 nano-needle is reduced by the high temperature (450 °C) calcination in a mixed atmosphere (5% H2 + 95% Ar) to form the Ni nanoparticle and MoO2 nano-needle, and this is confirmed by XRD and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Fig. S20–S21)... Raman proves the existing of CN, which can be ascribed to the reduction of organic carbon to CN [the ratio of area D and G (Area_D and Area_G) is 1.20], this is because the catalysis of Ni atoms (Fig. S22c).

the Ni/MoO₂@CN possesses good HER activity with low overpotentials (η_-10 = 33 mV, η_-1000 = 267 mV)... The Ni/MoO₂@CN exhibits a lower Tafel slope of 45 mV dec^-1... Ni/MoO₂@CN possesses the largest TOF value (1.45 s^-1) at the overpotential of 100 mV... Ni/MoO₂@CN exhibits the largest C_dl (97.94 mF)... displays outstanding durability at -1000 mA cm^-2 for 200 h

Ni/MoO₂@CN shows higher activity (η_10 = 250 mV, η_1000 = 420 mV)... displays the smallest Tafel slope... the TOF value of Ni/MoO₂@CN (1.23 s^-1) is higher... maintains good stability for 200 h at 1000 mA cm^-2 (Fig.6g); the change of potential is about 70 mV

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH at 30°C
nodes.source_text: Under 1.0 M KOH + 30 °C condition... Ni/MoO₂@CN (1.83 V)... at 200 mA cm^-2... drive the large current density of 500 and 1000 mA cm^-2 while only requiring 1.92 and 2.02 V... it can maintain for 300 h at 1000 mA cm^-2

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 6.0 M KOH at 60°C (industrial condition)
nodes.source_text: under the simulated industrial condition (6.0 M KOH + 60 °C)... it only requires 1.86 V for Ni/MoO₂@CN to reach 1000 mA cm^-2... It can work stably for 330 h at 1000 mA cm^-2 with negligible potential change
The volume–time curve for H₂ and O₂ is about 2:1, and they are close to the theoretical values, indicating the nearly 100% Faradic efficiency.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms the presence of Ni and MoO2 phases in the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder used for X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterization is obtained from NF... which can be determined by XRD (Supplementary Figure S19).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM confirms Ni nanoparticle and MoO2 nano-needle morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: this is confirmed by XRD and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Fig. S20–S21).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms presence of CN with AreaD/AreaG ratio of 1.20.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman proves the existing of CN... [the ratio of area D and G (AreaD and AreaG) is 1.20]

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ni nanoparticle (0.208 nm (111)) coupled with MoO2 nano-needle (0.242 nm (200)) with ~3 carbon layers on Ni and ~2 on MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the 0.208 nm (111) of Ni nanoparticle couples with the 0.242 nm (200) of MoO2 nano-needle... carbon layers are coated on the surface of Ni (≈3 layers, Fig. 4b) and MoO2 (≈2 layers, Fig. 4d)

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows clear heterojunction between Ni nanoparticle and MoO2 nano-needle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a clear heterojunction exists between the Ni nanoparticle and MoO2 nano-needle (Fig. 4c, d)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping show uniform distribution of C, N, O, Ni, and Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and elemental mapping images suggest the uniform distribution of C, N, O, Ni, and Mo

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Ni, C, Mo, N, O; Ni 2p shows positive shift ≈0.3 eV and ≈0.5 eV relative to Ni/MoO2 and Ni@CN respectively; Mo 3d shows negative shift ≈0.3 eV and ≈0.5 eV relative to Ni/MoO2 and MoO2@CN respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p and Mo 3d of Ni/MoO2@CN show a positive shift ≈0.3 eV... relative to Ni/MoO2... Furthermore, Ni 2p spectrum of Ni/MoO2@CN presents a positive shift ≈0.5 eV... relative to Ni@CN... Mo 3d spectrum of Ni/MoO2@CN exhibits a negative shift (≈0.5 eV) as against to MoO2@CN
